title: IMPLICIT BIAS-LIKE PATTERNS IN REASONING MODELS

bias_targets.methodology: Measuring the difference in reasoning token counts when reasoning models categorize European American versus African American names with pleasant versus unpleasant attributes in association-compatible versus association-incompatible instructions using the Reasoning Model Implicit Association Test (RM-IAT).

Comparing the computational effort (number of reasoning tokens) expended when models categorize male and female names/terms with stereotypical attributes (e.g., Career, Math, Science) versus counter-stereotypical attributes (e.g., Family, Arts) using the RM-IAT.
Evaluating the difference in reasoning token usage when models categorize terms representing young versus old people with pleasant versus unpleasant words using the RM-IAT.

Measuring reasoning token counts when categorizing mental versus physical diseases with temporary versus permanent attributes in association-compatible versus association-incompatible setups using the RM-IAT.
